scope: Research/proposal only for a sharable Rust core and Kedra OS composition; no implementation, migration, exploit reproduction or qualification.

claims.claim: The 2024 thesis assumes an attacker controlling the central repository, but not developer machines/private keys; availability and confidentiality are outside its update-integrity goal.
claims.confidence: high: author-defined scope

claims.claim: Commit signatures, verified ancestry with permissions, and reference-operation authentication provide distinct guarantees; the Git-Verify introduction is an external trust anchor, and unsigned automatic merges have a stated mix-and-match limitation.
claims.confidence: high: historical design, not current tool validation

claims.claim: Verification hidden inside a fixed-output fetch can be skipped by reuse of existing payload bytes. The author separates payload-plus-evidence download from ordinary verification for Git-Verify, but explicitly warns that the thesis's Gittuf fetcher retained this weakness.
claims.evidence: ba.pdf PDF29-30, printed27-28, section5.1.5 and figures5.1-5.3.
claims.confidence: high: dated author finding; not a reproduced present vulnerability

claims.claim: The proposed Niv anti-rollback check uses previous accepted ancestry and can reject branch/fork changes; signatures do not alone prevent replay or indefinite freeze.
claims.confidence: high: dated implementation and stated limits

provenance.identity_evidence: PDF1: Finn Landweber, HTWK Leipzig, 23 July 2024
provenance.focused_body_coverage: PDF16-32, chapters3-6; formal invariant, examples, diagrams and limits
provenance.limitation: PDF authoritative; supplied text read. No claim of remote-byte equivalence or current exploit reproduction.

claims.claim: Immutable parallel versions and a single profile-link replacement support local selection atomicity; distributed deployment adds build/closure transfer followed by activation.
claims.confidence: high: historical author model

claims.claim: The distributed atomicity argument requires exclusive cohort profile locks and proxies that drain old connections and block new ones throughout transition; installing packages alone is insufficient.
claims.confidence: high: explicit assumptions

claims.claim: The paper states rollback on commit failure but does not specify partition/coordinator-crash recovery sufficient to establish atomicity under arbitrary partial network failure; some services require explicit lifecycle operations beyond profile changes.
claims.evidence: atomic-hotswup2008-final.pdf PDF4, section5; PDF5, section7. First clause about missing failure protocol is review inference from this bounded paper.
claims.confidence: high for explicit lifecycle limitation; medium-high for completeness assessment

provenance.identity_evidence: PDF1 authors/title/HotSWUp08 imprint; DOI from archived official research index
provenance.limitation: No distributed experiment run; no fleet scope inferred.

claims.claim: Input-based output sharing requires common trust in substituted binaries. The intensional model separates content identity from per-user accepted recipe-to-output mappings; the mixed model permits selective trust. These historical user relations differ from today's root-equivalent trusted-users setting.
claims.evidence: secsharing-ase2005-final.pdf PDF4-9, sections2.3-5; modern setting is S-019.
claims.confidence: high: author model, not current implementation claim

claims.claim: Distinct concurrent builder UIDs, no direct user store writes and killing residual writers before changing ownership/modes prevent cross-build interference; chmod/chown alone cannot revoke an already-open writable descriptor.
claims.confidence: high: explicit security analysis

claims.claim: Validity excludes unfinished paths, requires valid dependencies and uses database transactions; simplified pseudocode deliberately omits implemented locking.
claims.confidence: high: historical implementation account

claims.claim: Self-references require normalized hashes and rewriting. The author's 86-component experiment succeeded but cannot establish universal compatibility: compressed/hidden references defeat scanning and rewriting, and collision resistance remains assumed.
claims.confidence: high: dated experiment and explicit limits

provenance.limitation: Original 2005 mechanisms and experiment, not current Nix behavior or modern compatibility evidence.

claims.claim: Derivations serialize to content-addressed objects; output addressing is independent. Creators supply explicit dependency inputs. Higher-order deriving paths are experimental.
claims.evidence: https://nix.dev/manual/nix/2.34/store/derivation/ : Inputs, Encoding, Extending the model to be higher-order.
claims.confidence: high: observed 2.34.9 documentation

claims.claim: Input addresses quotient over CA dependency identities and may await floating inputs. Fixed CA outputs check expected content; floating CA is experimental. Overview terminology is inconsistent, and the detailed IA page notes a possible experimental implementation/spec discrepancy.
claims.evidence: https://nix.dev/manual/nix/2.34/store/derivation/outputs/input-address : Modulo content addressed derivation outputs, Content-addressed outputs case; https://nix.dev/manual/nix/2.34/store/derivation/outputs/ ; https://nix.dev/manual/nix/2.34/store/derivation/outputs/content-address : Fixed-output, Floating, Floating versus Fixed.
claims.confidence: high for documented distinctions; exact experimental compatibility unverified

claims.claim: CA store identities incorporate data, references, name and store directory, with special self-reference normalization. The separate NAR hash covers filesystem serialization; integrity checking and accepted trust are different checks.
claims.confidence: high: documentation; source-correspondence/freshness distinction is synthesis

claims.claim: Reference closure and valid storage are required; cross-object cycles are forbidden. Builders lock outputs, normalize permissions and scan hashes. These do not establish complete semantic dependency discovery.
claims.evidence: https://nix.dev/manual/nix/2.34/store/store-object : References, Closure property; https://nix.dev/manual/nix/2.34/store/building : Builder Execution, Processing outputs. Dependency caveat also S-013 PDF9.
claims.confidence: high: docs plus stated historical caveat

claims.claim: Strings retain dependency contexts; discarding context discards tracking. Filesystem-dependent IFD can cause realisation during evaluation; it can be disabled. Experimental verified-fetches authenticates selected Git commits against keys, not a documented full freshness policy.
claims.confidence: high: 2.34.9 docs; policy limit is inference

claims.claim: Roots and generations retain dependency closures; indirect roots must retain their location. One profile link switches atomically. Public GC pages do not establish full concurrent acquisition/deletion ordering.
claims.confidence: high: described behavior; concurrency remains unverified

claims.claim: Direct local stores need no daemon; copying requires identical logical store paths. Unprivileged runtime-root discovery needs special consideration; an external roots daemon is experimental. Build directories must prevent other users' interference.
claims.confidence: high: documentation; no daemonless multi-user design qualified

claims.claim: Trusted daemon users have root-equivalent powers, unlike isolated builder identities. CA paths are exempt from ordinary signature requirements. Sandbox/fallback/platform settings matter; metadata fsync and payload fsync differ. Evaluator restriction is separate from builder sandboxing.
claims.evidence: https://nix.dev/manual/nix/2.34/command-ref/conf-file : trusted-users, trusted-public-keys, require-sigs, sandbox, sandbox-fallback, fsync-metadata, fsync-store-paths, pure-eval, restrict-eval; https://nix.dev/manual/nix/2.34/installation/multi-user .
claims.confidence: high: documented settings, not an audited host configuration

claims.claim: NAR encodes file data/executable flag, directories and symlinks, not owners, arbitrary modes, xattrs, labels or capabilities. A NAR digest therefore cannot attest complete Fedora security metadata. Store secrets are readable/shared and should be provisioned outside it at runtime.
claims.confidence: high: format evidence; Fedora consequence is explicit inference
